content.text: Speaking on the occasion, Professor Anita Ghulam Ali, the former Sindh Education Minister, urged that the valuable research commissioned by UNESCO and USAID on teacher education, accreditation and standards be shared widely if it is to be included both in education policy and its implementation. The recommendations of the workshop also need to be shared with policy makers, Sindh legislators, the Senate Standing Committee on Education and the Ministry of Education as the government is in the process of completing the new National Education Policy and these could provide useful inputs.

The panelists at the workshop shared their experiences and stressed on the need for merit-based recruitment of teachers, adding that teacher resource centers and networks operating in the private and public sectors should be ' institutionalised' and provided with dedicated staff and financing. Innovations in resource or professional development should be replicated by the government through public sector funds with an emphasis on internet and communication technologies. Efficient internet services should be made available to government high schools and teacher training colleges to allow students and teachers access to professional opportunities and to sustain networks. The panelists also suggested that Provincial Institutes of Teacher Education (PITE), the Bureau of Curriculum and the government Elementary Colleges of Education should develop a strong team with expertise in distance education, learning technologies and Information Communication Technologies. Teachers should be encouraged to be creative, through pre and in-service programmes, and they should be provided with copies of the new National Curriculum 2006, especially at the high and middle school level and in taluka- and district-level institutions, both in Urdu and Sindhi.

Panelists were drawn form various educational networks and associations, including Professional Teacher Association Network, City District Government, Karachi, Bureau of Curriculum, PITE, Nawabshah, Sindh Education Foundation, Society of Pakistan English Language Teachers (SPELT), ED-LINKS, Teachers Resource Centre, International Education and Resource Network (iEARN), INTEL and Indus Resource Centre. They presented diverse experiences from the public and the private sectors.

The new Anita Ghulam Ali Teachers' Award was also launched at the workshop. The Award will recognise secondary level teachers (grade IX-X) and secondary school head teachers in the country for their efforts towards school improvement. content.title: World Teachers Day 2008
content.author: volunteer.pa
content.description: Raising the status of teachers requires continuous professional development, which can be undertaken by adopting new technologies and improving existing teacher networks. This was the conclusion of a day-long workshop on World Teachers' Day at Aga Khan University's Institute for Educational Development by the Idara-e-Taleem-o-Aagahi in collaboration with AKU-IED and UNESCO, Pakistan. The event was attended by over 80 teachers and educators from Sindh.
